User story: As an operator, I want loom commands to open the correct local or cloud FleetDB store so issue state is consistent across CLI, daemon, and web UI.
Expected behavior: Store open resolves from config/env/workspace state, supports embedded FleetDB when requested, caches mode metadata, and fails with actionable diagnostics when the backend is unavailable.
Notes: Local and cloud paths inspected from source; no live backend smoke run in this pass.

User story: As a CLI user, I want every loom subcommand to share config, workspace, and output handling so commands behave predictably.
Expected behavior: Root command wires config loading, output format flags, workspace context, and shared clients before delegating to feature subcommands.
Notes: README examples should be checked when command syntax changes.

User story: As a local operator, I want to create, list, select, and inspect workspaces from the CLI so I can switch Loom contexts safely.
Expected behavior: Workspace commands manage workspace records, active selection, local paths, and JSON output without silently mutating unrelated workspaces.
Notes: Workspace CRUD refs/tests exist; README drift is tracked on the affected repo, role, and daemon profile rows.

User story: As a project lead, I want workspace diagnostics to explain readiness blockers so I know whether agents can pick up work.
Expected behavior: Diagnostics report backend reachability, local runtime health, agents, worktrees, queue status, and actionable problem codes; ensure-runtime prepares missing runtime prerequisites.
Notes: This is the readiness authority used by existing Loom lead runbooks.

User story: As an operator, I want to register repositories and prepare worktrees so agents can run against the intended codebase.
Expected behavior: Repo commands add/list/show/remove repositories, resolve default branches, and checkout or prepare local worktrees without losing user changes.
Defect status: Open: README command examples drift from current Cobra syntax
Notes: README still shows `repo add <name> --url ...`; current command expects `repo add <NAME> <REMOTE_URL>`.

User story: As an administrator, I want to define agent roles and limits so task routing can enforce appropriate capabilities.
Expected behavior: Role commands add/list/show/remove roles and set/unset supported policy fields such as model, backend, effort, task filters, priority/concurrency/budget limits, read-only mode, skills, path patterns, and allowed/denied tools.
Defect status: Open: README role examples use obsolete role set/unset flag syntax
Notes: No direct role CLI unit tests found; indirect daemon/task-router tests cover role constraint consumption.

User story: As an administrator, I want to manage agent definitions and start or stop them so work is assigned to the intended runtime profile.
Expected behavior: Agent definition commands add/list/show/remove/start/stop assignments, persist role, backend, repo/repo-group, cross-repo, parent, mode, task filter, max-concurrency, budget policy, auto-start, and desired-state fields, create local worktrees when workspace-local repo paths are known, and enqueue start/stop commands when the command store is available.
Notes: No agentdef update command or queued-start list/cancel CLI found; direct agentdef command coverage not found.

User story: As an operator, I want to configure daemon runtime profile fields so the local daemon runs with the intended paths, backend mode, capacity, and startup timeout.
Expected behavior: Daemon profile commands show, set, and unset the daemon-profile fields currently exposed by the CLI: pid_file, log_dir, events_dir, issue_backend, max_agents, and startup_timeout; unsupported keys fail with an unknown-key error.
Defect status: Open: README daemon profile examples drift from current Cobra syntax
Notes: No focused daemon profile set/unset tests found; README still shows stale flag-style daemon profile examples.

Feature: Supervisor lifecycle, logs, control, and queue
User story: As a lead, I want daemon commands and APIs to start, stop, inspect, and drain agents so I can operate the local runtime.
Expected behavior: Daemon control surfaces expose status, logs, start/stop/restart, queue state, stuck-agent detection, and safe cancellation.
Notes: Manual runtime validation should use `.agent-skills/loom-pr-test/SKILL.md`.

User story: As a contributor, I want `loom data` read commands to show ready, blocked, review, and monitor views so I can pick the right work.
Expected behavior: Read commands apply status/type/parent/assignee filters, support JSON output, and do not mutate issue state.
Notes: This is central to agent handoff and lead startup checks.

User story: As an agent, I want to claim, update, block, release, and close issues so the queue reflects real work state.
Expected behavior: Write commands enforce backend contracts, optimistic update semantics, assignee transitions, status changes, and close reasons.
Notes: Cross-backend claim/release parity should stay covered as FleetDB evolves.

Feature: Server agent control via data agent
User story: As a lead, I want to list and control agents through the configured Loom server so I can operate a running workspace from the CLI.
Expected behavior: `loom data agents` lists server-reported agents, and `loom data agent` start/stop/restart/yield POSTs to `/api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/{action}`, including force-stop bodies and clear daemon/HTTP/error-envelope failures.
Notes: No data-agent CLI lease/heartbeat show command found; this is server agent control, not direct FleetDB lease admin.

Feature: Git push, pull, sync, and conflict handling
User story: As an agent, I want Loom git commands to synchronize work safely so local changes reach the remote without overwriting others.
Expected behavior: Git APIs and CLI commands report status, handle pull/rebase/push flows, surface conflicts, and keep issue/worktree context attached.
Notes: Manual conflict-path validation remains important before release.

User story: As an operator, I want reset commands to make destructive scope explicit so accidental data loss is avoided.
Expected behavior: Reset surfaces require explicit target/default branch and confirmation/force for destructive paths, respect active-agent lock and protected-branch safeguards, and avoid deleting unrelated workspace state.
Notes: Destructive-path review should be repeated when reset UX changes.

User story: As an agent, I want to create and list pull requests from Loom so completed work can move to code review.
Expected behavior: PR commands and UI handlers detect remotes and branches, push source branches, create or reuse GitHub PRs with generated titles/bodies, list PR state including draft/review metadata from gh, and surface gh/API errors.
Notes: Live GitHub checks require network credentials and were not run; PR creation has no draft/final flag or linked-issue metadata in the inspected CLI code.

Feature: Worker profiles, services, and remote worker admin
User story: As an operator, I want to configure local and remote worker capacity so tasks route to healthy executors.
Expected behavior: Worker commands/services expose worker profiles, agent service desired state and placement fields, workspace-name resolution, remote worker registration/deregistration, lock-state updates, event forwarding, and log forwarding.
Notes: No heartbeat/worktree-readiness worker admin surface found; distributed smoke remains the best end-to-end confidence signal.

User story: As a maintainer, I want quality-gate targets to validate Go, frontend, generated API state, workflow tests, and API e2e paths before changes land.
Expected behavior: `make gate` runs check-go and check-frontend; check-go includes generated API staleness and clean-env Go tests, check-frontend runs frontend format/type/lint/generated/unit coverage checks, while workflow bundle tests and API e2e run separately through make test-builtin-workflows and make test-e2e-api.
Automated coverage: make gate; make check-go; make check-frontend; make test-builtin-workflows; make test-e2e-api
Notes: Commands were not run in this audit; make gate does not include test-builtin-workflows or test-e2e-api.

Feature: Web app auth and config boot
User story: As a browser user, I want the app to load config, auth state, and workspace context before showing protected workspace UI.
Expected behavior: App boot fetches config, handles loading/error states, gates protected routes, and initializes workspace-aware clients.
Notes: Auth service behavior is mapped separately.

User story: As a user, I want the web app to route me into a selected workspace or let me create one when none exists.
Expected behavior: Root routes redirect to the active workspace, create flow submits valid workspace data, and navigation preserves workspace IDs in URLs and API calls.
Notes: FleetDB UI route smoke should cover this against a real stack.

User story: As a user, I want to browse workspace repositories and issue groupings so I can narrow work by repo or area.
Expected behavior: Tree state loads workspace repositories, filters issues by repo/path, and keeps selected context stable across navigation.
Notes: Manual usability pass should verify large workspaces remain scannable.

User story: As a contributor, I want to view issues as kanban, list, or table so I can work in the layout that fits the task.
Expected behavior: Views share issue data, status buckets, sorting, grouping, selection, and route state without losing filters.
Test status: Automated coverage found; not run; Needs coverage
Notes: Real FleetDB UI coverage exists but was not executed; list view behavior needs focused coverage.

User story: As a contributor, I want to create, edit, claim, close, and reopen issues from the UI so queue state stays current.
Expected behavior: UI and APIs validate issue fields, status transitions, assignee changes, optimistic updates, and error recovery; backend delete remains an API route but is not exposed as a mapped UI action.
Notes: Issue lifecycle is one of the best-covered UI slices by existing FleetDB specs.

Feature: Search, filter, and group URL sync
User story: As a user, I want search and filters to be bookmarkable so I can share and revisit focused work views.
Expected behavior: Search text, labels, priority/type filters, repo selection, grouping, and blocked visibility round-trip through URL/query state and API filters where supported; table sort remains local UI state.
Notes: Validate deep-link compatibility when adding new filters.

User story: As a lead, I want to see issue dependencies and blockers so I can understand what prevents work from starting.
Expected behavior: Dependency APIs and graph views create/remove links, render blocked relationships, and update affected issue cards.
Notes: Manual graph review should include dense dependency sets.

User story: As a collaborator, I want comments and event history on issues so handoffs preserve context.
Expected behavior: Comments can be added, listed, and rendered with author/time metadata; issue events record lifecycle changes and remain ordered.
Notes: Audit retention and pagination were not live-tested.

User story: As a user, I want the board and detail views to update when other agents change issues so I do not work from stale state.
Expected behavior: SSE connection subscribes per workspace, handles reconnect/backoff, applies issue events idempotently, and surfaces connection errors.
Notes: Reconnect paths have explicit FleetDB specs but were not executed.

User story: As an agent operator, I want terminal tabs to attach to live or historical sessions so I can inspect and resume work.
Expected behavior: Terminal routes issue tokens, open WebSocket sessions, load tab metadata, reconnect to agent terminals, and expose setup/state endpoints.
Notes: Terminal API docs drift is tracked in LCLI-049; use real runtime runbook for terminal evidence.

User story: As a reviewer, I want session transcripts and diffs linked to issues so I can verify what an agent changed.
Expected behavior: Session APIs list runs, expose transcript chunks, show diff summaries, and tie artifacts to the correct workspace and issue.
Notes: AGENTS explicitly forbids fake transcripts/diffs as evidence.

Feature: Agent detail, work panels, and lifecycle controls
User story: As a lead, I want agent detail panels to show status and controls so I can route or stop work.
Expected behavior: Agent pages show definitions, live status, assigned work, sessions, branch/worktree details, terminal links, and safe action controls.
Notes: UI-created agent routing still needs local-mode verification for end-to-end pickup.

Feature: Git, diff, and file review in UI
User story: As a reviewer, I want UI git status and diffs so I can inspect an agent branch before PR or merge.
Expected behavior: UI git routes show branch/status, ahead/behind counts, push/pull/sync/PR/reset actions, target-branch changes, diff file lists and patches, and conflict/error states for the selected agent/workspace.
Notes: Manual conflict and binary-file cases remain useful.

User story: As a reviewer, I want a PR view linked to Loom work so review status is visible in the workspace.
Expected behavior: PR page lists pull requests, links them to repositories/issues, shows status, and handles GitHub API errors.
Notes: Live GitHub credentials are required for full validation.

User story: As a developer, I want to browse workspace files and open them in my editor so I can inspect context quickly.
Expected behavior: File APIs list trees, read file contents, save permitted edits, and launch configured editors without exposing paths outside the workspace.
Notes: Path traversal and editor launch cases should stay security-reviewed.

User story: As an operator, I want monitor and observability pages so I can understand runtime health, queues, metrics, and traces.
Expected behavior: Dashboards load monitor snapshots, metrics, event streams, task/run state, and error summaries with clear empty/error states.
Notes: Production metrics quality is mapped separately under events/tracing; usage dashboard is tracked in LCLI-059.

Feature: Settings backend and local runtime config
User story: As an operator, I want settings to manage backend and local runtime configuration so Loom points at the right services.
Expected behavior: Settings load and update local settings, FleetDB backend config, AI backend setup, notify token status, and runtime toggles with validation.
Notes: Backend config docs drift is tracked in LCLI-049.

User story: As a new user, I want onboarding to set up a first workspace/task so Loom becomes usable without CLI setup.
Expected behavior: Onboarding detects first-run state, guides required setup, submits first task creation, and transitions into the workspace view.
Defect status: Open: web-onboarding spec status endpoints are not registered
Notes: Spec references `GET /api/onboarding/status` and `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/onboarding/status`; current implementation uses client-side first-run detection plus POST first-task.

User story: As a workflow runner, I want driver runs to claim, execute, heartbeat, complete, or fail predictably so workflow state is auditable.
Expected behavior: Driver creates run records, claims work, executes steps, records heartbeats/logs/results, and releases or fails runs on errors.
Notes: Run lifecycle is core platform behavior; keep cross-store regression tests current.

User story: As an operator, I want workflow runtimes authenticated with run-scoped tokens so one run cannot operate another run.
Expected behavior: Serve mints LOOM_RUN_TOKEN at claim, driver-op APIs validate bearer token scope, and legacy node-wide token fallback is controlled by rollout env.
Notes: Deploy notes say LOOM_DRIVER_API_TOKEN fallback is temporary and should be removed after SDK rollout.

Feature: Sandbox trust placement and container egress
User story: As a platform operator, I want untrusted workflows isolated with bounded egress so workflow code cannot access unauthorized services.
Expected behavior: Untrusted drivers fail closed outside an isolating launcher, trusted placement is explicit, container mode enforces caps, and egress mode records mechanism and reachability.
Test status: Automated coverage found; not run; Manual pending
Notes: Native Linux podman is required for the full relay/network isolation acceptance leg.

User story: As a workflow author, I want the SDK to call driver-op APIs with the right headers and tokens so bundles do not depend on FleetDB credentials.
Expected behavior: SDK resolves driver API URL/token from env, sends run-scoped auth, surfaces typed errors, and avoids direct FleetDB when serve API is available.
Automated coverage: sdk/driver.test.mjs; sdk/contract.test.mjs; sdk/runtime-adapters.test.mjs; npm --prefix sdk test
Notes: Task-run wrappers should stop provisioning LOOM_FLEET_DB_URL/API_KEY when serve bridge exists.

User story: As a task runner, I want a serve-hosted task-run API protected by per-run lease token so runners can report artifacts without FleetDB secrets.
Expected behavior: Serve exposes `/api/workspaces/{ws}/task-run/{op}`, validates lease token, bridges artifacts/logs/status, and exports LOOM_TASK_RUN_API_URL to spawned runners.
Notes: Need CI coverage that verifies SDK fallback is not used when serve bridge exists.

User story: As a lead, I want task runs scheduled to eligible workers with retry/error semantics so work progresses reliably.
Expected behavior: Scheduler selects available workers, records leases, handles retryable failures, marks terminal failures, and exposes queue state.
Notes: Live queue readiness should be checked before blaming agents for not picking up tasks.

Feature: Runner artifacts, transcripts, and patch evidence
User story: As a reviewer, I want task-run artifacts to contain real logs, transcripts, diffs, and patches so completion evidence is trustworthy.
Expected behavior: Runners stream logs, persist artifacts, record transcripts/diffs from actual sessions, and expose patchbacks without accepting fabricated state.
Notes: AGENTS forbids manually creating fake lock files, FleetDB state, sessions, transcripts, diffs, or evidence.

Feature: Built-in workflow registration and source validation
User story: As a maintainer, I want built-in workflows registered from source and validated so generated bundles do not drift into git.
Expected behavior: Built-ins load from source, preserve trusted stamps where appropriate, validate Flue source layout, and keep generated dist artifacts out of version control.
Notes: AGENTS says edit `internal/workflows/builtin/`, not generated `builtin-dist`.

User story: As a lead, I want the epic runner to decompose and route child work so larger initiatives progress through agents and review.
Expected behavior: Epic runner creates child issues, links dependencies, launches or assigns agents, monitors child completion, and reports final epic status.
Notes: Real runtime validation should avoid starting duplicate runs when backend assignment already exists.

User story: As an operator, I want local and Daytona runners to execute task runs in the correct environment so agents can work both locally and remotely.
Expected behavior: Runners prepare worktrees, inject scoped env, start approved CLIs, stream output, and report lifecycle state back to Loom.
Test status: Automated coverage found; not run; Manual pending
Notes: Local-mode and Codex local-mode checks were identified but not executed.

Feature: External auth service and JWT validation
User story: As a deployment operator, I want the auth service to issue and validate tokens so web/API access can be protected in shared deployments.
Expected behavior: Service validates env schema, supports login/session/JWT flows, exposes health, and documents secure deployment configuration.
Notes: Auth service tests are separate from the main Go/frontend gate unless invoked explicitly.

User story: As a maintainer, I want the local-mode stack to prove real local agents can pick up configured work so demos reflect production behavior.
Expected behavior: Local-mode scripts launch FleetDB, serve, web UI, and local agents; verification polls seeded/configured planner/coder tasks via API and observes agent pickup/completion, sessions, transcripts, and diffs.
Automated coverage: make local-mode-up; make local-mode-verify; make local-mode-codex-up; make local-mode-codex-verify
Test status: Automated coverage found; not run; Manual pending
Notes: Runbook requires real runtime/browser evidence; not run during mapping.

Feature: FleetDB UI routing proof and distributed smoke
User story: As a maintainer, I want real FleetDB UI and distributed smoke tests so browser workflows and remote routing do not regress.
Expected behavior: FleetDB UI regression runs against a prepared real FleetDB-backed stack with preflight/routing proof; distributed smoke builds and starts real services and verifies claim contention, SSE reconnect, cross-node transcripts, and WebUI health.
Automated coverage: make test-fleetdb-ui; make test-distributed-smoke; make gate-e2e-full
Notes: Existing Playwright specs map many UI stories, but full smoke was not executed.

Feature: Generated API staleness and SDK contracts
User story: As a maintainer, I want generated API clients and docs to match registered routes so frontend and SDK consumers do not call stale endpoints.
Expected behavior: OpenAPI generation and committed frontend/Go clients are checked for staleness against api/openapi.yaml, and SDK contract tests freeze driver-op paths/error envelopes; route/docs drift still requires static comparison against registered routes.
Automated coverage: make check-go-api-staleness; npm --prefix internal/webui/frontend run check:generated; sdk/contract.test.mjs; npm --prefix sdk test
Defect status: Open: docs/API and OpenAPI route inventory drift for terminal lifecycle and backend config
Notes: Terminal lifecycle docs/OpenAPI and project-level backend config docs cite routes not registered by current modules; onboarding status spec drift is tracked in LCLI-035.

User story: As an operator, I want events, traces, and metrics to explain system behavior so runtime failures can be triaged quickly.
Expected behavior: Events are recorded consistently, metrics expose useful labels without cardinality blowups, and observability APIs replay or query recent activity.
Notes: Map to dashboard row LCLI-033 for browser presentation; this row tracks backend signal quality.

User story: As an operator, I want Loom backend definitions to invoke supported agent CLIs consistently so local and remote agents run with the intended model, effort, sandbox, and transcript behavior.
Expected behavior: Backend registry and wrappers construct Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Opencode, Echo, and external backend invocations, expose capabilities, enforce process guards, and normalize invocation errors.
Notes: Live third-party backend CLIs were not run in this audit.

User story: As an agent operator, I want Loom to run task agents, automode loops, and lead sessions so issue work can be claimed, executed, recovered, and completed.
Expected behavior: Agent commands build prompts, claim/release tasks, emit session events, run backend CLIs, support automode polling/yield/recovery, and provide lead-mode orchestration.
Notes: Real agent execution evidence should follow `.agent-skills/loom-pr-test/SKILL.md`.

Feature: Connector vault, grants, dispatch, and rotation
User story: As an operator, I want external connector credentials and grants managed safely so workflows can call approved services without exposing secrets.
Expected behavior: Connector commands and services store vault secrets, resolve provider grants, dispatch approved connector calls, rotate credentials, and keep provider-specific behavior testable.
Notes: Provider-specific Datadog, GitHub, and Slack tests exist; no live external connector calls were run.

User story: As an integrator, I want triggers and webhooks to convert external or internal events into Loom workflow actions so automation can start from repository and issue events.
Expected behavior: Trigger commands store patterns, bridge issue-journal events, match await subjects, track cursor state, and webhook handlers verify/route GitHub deliveries into workflow dispatch.
Notes: Live webhook delivery from GitHub was not run.

User story: As a workflow author, I want approval and await gates so workflows can pause until authorized or until matching external events arrive.
Expected behavior: Driver await operations create durable await records, resume or time out waits, match trigger subjects, and preserve approval gate state for controlled continuation.
Notes: Approval/await behavior is part of workflow correctness and authorization boundaries.

User story: As a workflow author, I want workflow registration, preflight, and driver APIs so custom workflows can be validated and run through Loom.
Expected behavior: Workflow endpoints list built-ins, preflight workflow definitions, register driver tasks, accept task requests, and expose driver API workflow operations with typed errors.
Notes: Live custom workflow submission was not run.

User story: As a reviewer, I want stacked branches published and restacked predictably so multi-commit work can be reviewed as an ordered PR stack.
Expected behavior: Stack publishing derives branch lineage, plans stack order, pushes/restacks branches, reconciles GitHub PRs, and stores stack metadata for later updates.
Notes: Live GitHub stack publishing requires credentials and was not run.

User story: As a workspace administrator, I want to rename, delete, reorder, and configure workspaces in the UI/API so the workspace list stays manageable after initial creation.
Expected behavior: Workspace APIs support listing, creating, renaming, deleting, reordering, default selection, backend config, and job/status reads; UI surfaces switcher and workspace page workflows.
Notes: Redirect/create is tracked separately in LCLI-019.

User story: As an operator, I want usage data summarized and cleaned up so I can monitor cost trends without retaining stale local records forever.
Expected behavior: Usage collectors append session usage records, serve aggregated usage API responses, render a usage dashboard, and cleanup commands purge old usage/session/event records.
Notes: Usage cleanup is local data-retention behavior; no live dashboard smoke was run.
